blocks.text: Small apartment: how to make every meter count

parts.html: In a small apartment, every square meter counts. Below are the techniques we use most often when designing small apartments and studios.

Start with the layout: divide the apartment into functional zones for the kitchen, living room, bedroom, and workspace. Movable partitions, sliding doors, or dual-purpose furniture all work for this. In a studio apartment, the kitchen and living room are separated with a breakfast bar, a sofa with its back to the kitchen, or different lighting.
Wall beds, sofa beds, and convertible tables save space and adapt to different needs. A bed that folds into a cabinet during the day turns the bedroom into a spacious living room or home office.

Storage is the main problem in small apartments. Use the height of the room: ceiling-high shelves, cabinets, and overhead storage hold more without taking up floor space. Hidden storage can go under the bed and sofa, with organizers and containers to keep things in order inside. Custom built-in wardrobes are made to the exact size of alcoves and wall sections, with no empty gaps at the sides.

Light and color make a space look bigger. Light walls, floors, and furniture together with daylight make a room feel open, and a mirror opposite the window adds to the effect. Make the main lighting bright and even, while table lamps and wall sconces give soft evening light and pick out individual zones.

Choose compact appliances: a two- or three-burner cooktop, a narrow 45 cm dishwasher, an oven with a microwave function. Arrange cabinets and shelves so that everything you need is within reach, and put the folding table and chairs away when you are not using them.

You can find room for storage here too: shelves above the door, a cabinet under the sink, corner shelves. Mirrored cabinets and light-colored finishes will make the bathroom look roomier and brighter.
Light, sheer curtains, small rugs, and minimal decor create a sense of lightness and air. Avoid large, bulky decor — it overwhelms the space.

Folding chairs, tables on casters, and mobile cabinets are easy to move around: during the day the table stands by the window as a desk, and in the evening it gets rolled over to the sofa. This helps most in studio apartments.

blocks.text: Making the most of corners and niches

parts.html: Corners and alcoves often sit empty, even though they can take corner shelves, a cabinet, or shelving built into the alcove.
The fewer things in a room, the more spacious it feels. Keep what you use every day, and limit decor to two or three pieces you really like.
Let one zone do several jobs: a table in the living room serves for both dining and work, and a sofa bed is a place to relax by day and to sleep at night.

Light and neutral colors make a space look bigger, but an interior that is entirely beige looks dull. Two or three bright pieces, such as cushions, a rug, or a painting, add color and are easy to swap.
Even a small apartment has room for plants: pick compact, low-maintenance ones and put them in wall planters and hanging pots so they don’t take up usable floor space.
